The ledger uses new receipts without reusing old onesFrom the supplied inventory, charge, and phi_from definitions, adding an endpoint-disjoint original  $A$  gives
$$\Delta\Phi
=
\max(0,-\operatorname{charge}(A))
+\mathbf 1_{\{\operatorname{charge}(A)>0\}}
+2|\mathcal F_{\rm new}|-|\mathcal E_{\rm new}|.
\tag{A}$$
This subtraction is legitimate because:Every retained original’s charge depends only on its own immutable record.An old directed event remains an event: its source owner, endpoints, support exclusions, and physical tile do not change.An old mixed full tile remains mixed. Endpoint disjointness prevents the new original from taking over its occupied cells.Thus the proof must identify the genuinely new mixed full tiles and source-labelled events. The supplied mathematical lists do that correctly.2. The actual- $q$ -owner exhaustion is completePut  $C=h+13$ . Direct substitution gives the three decisive retained records:
$$\begin{aligned}
P_0 &: (r,c)\longmapsto(23+r,C-c),\\
K &: (r,c)\longmapsto(25+r,C+c),\\
B_0[4] &: (r,c)\longmapsto(35-r,h+7+c).
\end{aligned}$$
Consequently,
$$\begin{aligned}
&(r,C-1)\in P_0 &&(23\le r\le33),\\
&(r,C+1)\in K &&(25\le r\le31),\\
&(31,C)\in B_0[4].
\end{aligned}
\tag{B}$$
These are uniform in  $h,g$ .For the canonical U constructor, the endpoint set is
$$\bigl(\{0,1\}\times\{1,\ldots,B\}\bigr)
\cup\bigl(\{2,\ldots,d\}\times\{1\}\bigr)
\cup\bigl(\{2,\ldots,f\}\times\{B\}\bigr).$$
Its degree-one vertices are the leg terminals; its degree-two vertices are the straight leg interiors and the two outer bar corners; all other bar vertices have degree three. Since north and west of  $q$  already belong to retained owners, the only possible internal-neighbour sets at  $q$  are
$$\{S\},\qquad \{E\},\qquad \{S,E\}.$$
The exclusions then work exactly as stated:A south terminal of depth at least eight contains  $(31,C)$ .Depths four and six put an adjacent bar endpoint at  $(26,C\pm1)$  or  $(28,C\pm1)$ , all blocked by (B).A downward outer-bar corner contains  $(25,C+1)$ .The remaining outer-corner orientation is the rightward family (2).The rotor exclusion also checks out directly from the supplied eight-endpoint rotor. Its nonterminal vertices have degree three. For terminals, the two south-neighbour patterns both contain relative endpoint  $(2,1)$ ; the two east-neighbour patterns are blocked by relative endpoints  $(-1,1)$  and  $(2,1)$ , respectively. These hit  $V$  or  $K$  as claimed.Finally, exchanging U legs preserves the complete source record, including the matching and alternating lateral supports: the reflection  $c\mapsto L+1-c$  sends  $U(L,d,f)$  to  $U(L,f,d)$ . Therefore the two east-terminal frames in (4) exhaust the remaining possibilities without losing a source phase.3. The entire feasible corner family has no complete extensionFor
$$Q:(r,c)\longmapsto(23+r,C-1+c),$$
endpoint disjointness is exactly
$$B\ge8,\qquad d\in\{4,6\},\qquad f\ge4,$$
with all parameters even: $B=6$  makes the far stem meet the root at row  $25$ . $d\ge8$  makes the near stem meet  $(31,C)$ .Under the displayed restrictions, the far column is at least  $h+20$ , the near stem stops before row  $31$ , and the bar occupies rows  $23,24$ , where the retained endpoints do not intersect it.The missing axial support
$$p=(24+d,C)$$
is indeed an immutable original support of  $Q$ , absent from  $H+Q$ .For  $d=6$ , all four neighbours of  $p=(30,C)$  are already retained endpoints. Any owner of  $p$  would need an own matching neighbour, and none is available.For  $d=4$ , the three retained neighbours of  $p=(28,C)$  leave only the south direction available. No other U or rotor role fits the three-neighbour gate.This excludes every member of the endpoint-disjoint corner family, independently of  $B,f,h,g$ . Additional owners in a proposed complete extension cannot remove these retained collisions.The comparison ledger is also correct. Direct source counting gives
$$\operatorname{charge}(Q)=1-B,$$
and the new receipt counts are
$$|\mathcal F_{\rm new}|=7+\frac{d-4}{2},
\qquad
|\mathcal E_{\rm new}|=20+d-4.$$
Hence
$$\Delta\Phi
=(B-1)+2\left(7+\frac{d-4}{2}\right)-(20+d-4)
=B-7.$$
This remains a partial-union calculation; the nonextension proof correctly prevents assigning it to an actual corner-owner occurrence.4. The upward identity is exactly  $2-\eta$ The source phases in (6) are correct. t=\frac L2+\frac{d+f}{2},\qquad

giving charge  $-1$  and exactly one unit of new negative mass.The endpoint-disjointness classification is exhaustive:For  $L=6$ , the far row is  $18$ , and avoiding  $V$ 's columns  $h+14,h+15$  requires the odd terminal

The horizontal  $P_0/A_{\rm up}$  directions are excluded by their respective immutable bar-end and axial supports. The near contribution, including the new negative mass, is therefore

For  $L=8$ , the far support phases give exactly the stated profiles:Far terminal  $e$ New full tilesNew events $2F-E$  $e\ge h+17$ 000 $e=h+15$ 01 $-1$  $e=h+13$ 13 $-1$  $e\le h+11$ 25 $-1$ In particular, the missing endpoint  $(17,h+10)$  correctly prevents an additional full tile on the left. These far receipts occupy row- $16$  tiles and cannot overlap the row- $22$  near receipts.Consequently,
$$\Delta\Phi(A_{\rm up}\mid H)
=2-\mathbf1_{\{L=8,\ d-f\le2\}}.$$
5. The downward frontier and  $3-\delta$  identity hold for all parametersThe row-frontier table can be derived uniformly, without using the finite controls. For one nine-original base with parameters  $(a,s,w,z)$ , write  $t=r-a$ . The emerging second base stays dominated by the first long stem until the second rotor takes over with maxima  $3,5$  on rows  $g+48,g+49$ . The final second-base stem ends exactly at row  $2g+67$ . The additional originals do not increase these maxima. This also covers  $g=4$ ; there is no omitted short-parameter transition.Thus the invariant
$$A\text{ even}\Rightarrow B\le A,\qquad
A\text{ odd}\Rightarrow B\le A+2,\qquad
A=\varnothing\Rightarrow B=\varnothing

is established.For  $A_{\rm down}$ , depths  $d=4,6$  make its bar meet the root at row  $25$ . If  $d\ge8$ , its bar begins at column  $h+20$  or farther right, across a physical-tile boundary from all retained endpoints. $$m=L-1+\frac{d+f}{2},\qquad
t=\frac L2+1+\frac{d+f}{2},\qquad
s_{\rm in}=4+\frac{d+f}{2}.$$

At  $h+13$  and  $h+15$ , both vertical directions are excluded by immutable supports. Its contribution, including the new positive-owner count, is

For the arbitrary far return, (C) leaves only the following possibilities: $A$  even: only  $e=A+1$  can contact an old endpoint. The sole candidate is the horizontal old-to-new event. Its reverse targets the new axial support. Since  $B\le A$ , no vertical event or full tile occurs. $A$  odd: only  $e=A+2$  can contact an old endpoint. The sole candidate is the vertical old-to-new event from  $(y+1,e)$ , if present. Its reverse targets the new far-leg lateral support. The absent upper cell at  $e-1>A$  prevents a full tile.Larger  $e$ , or an empty frontier, produces no far receipt.Testing that candidate against its retained source owner’s immutable support is exactly the required definition of  $\delta$ . Hence the far receipt has no new full tile and exactly  $\delta\in\{0,1\}$  new events. Its tiles are disjoint from the near receipt, proving
$$\Delta\Phi(A_{\rm down}\mid H)=3-\delta\ge2.$$
